points.t: A young adult with many moles (over 100 is the significant count), several atypical ones (≥5 mm, irregular, varied colour), and a family history of melanoma.
Inherited susceptibility (CDKN2A, CDK4 and others) plus sun exposure; atypical naevi are markers of risk more than precursors.

Refer to dermatology for baseline photography and risk-tailored surveillance; clinical genetics referral for several affected relatives, early-onset or multiple melanomas, or melanoma with pancreatic cancer in the family; monthly self-examination.
Melanoma among many atypical moles; pancreatic cancer risk in CDKN2A carriers.

items.t: Multiple atypical naevi with a family history of melanoma: refer to a **dermatology surveillance** service (NICE NG14).
Melanoma and pancreatic cancer in the same family: refer to **clinical genetics** (CDKN2A).

pearls.t: The PE teacher has an outdoor occupation: shade during outdoor lessons, long-sleeved UV tops, a hat, SPF 30–50 reapplied every 2 h and after sweating. The employer has duties (HSE outdoor workers' advice).
Explain that **most melanomas in AMS arise de novo, not from existing moles**. That is why whole-skin self-checks matter more than watching one mole.
